headline: arXivLabs framework for hybrid reasoning LLM agents launched
summary: New framework allows collaborators to develop and share new arXiv features directly on the website, focusing on hybrid reasoning agents that think in latent space.
details: arXiv has launched arXivLabs, a new framework designed to foster collaboration and innovation directly on its platform. This initiative allows external individuals and organizations to develop and share new features for arXiv.

A key focus of arXivLabs is the development of hybrid reasoning agents. These advanced AI agents are capable of thinking within a latent space and acting through text, representing a significant step forward in AI research.
The framework emphasizes arXiv's core values of openness, community, excellence, and user data privacy. arXiv is committed to partnering only with entities that uphold these principles.
Researchers and developers interested in contributing can learn more about the arXivLabs program and submit their ideas for projects that aim to enhance the arXiv community's experience.

headline_marked: Anthropic [[commits 5% of shares]] to a public benefit fund
headline: Anthropic commits 5% of shares to a public benefit fund
summary: The AI company is creating a fund to support societal good projects, with options to increase contributions based on company value.
details: Anthropic has announced the creation of a "public benefit fund" designed to provide the company with greater flexibility and scale to support projects aimed at societal good.

The AI firm will commit 5% of its shares to this fund, which will operate as a wholly-owned entity within Anthropic. There is also an option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic's value.

Potential uses for the fund include significant donations to traditional non-profits or direct distributions to specific populations. The company noted that given the rapid pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be necessary.
This initiative comes at a time when the AI industry is facing growing public skepticism, a situation CEO Dario Amodei has characterized as a "fundamentally a crisis of trust."
Anthropic has already committed $200 million to study the impact of AI on the job market, but the new fund offers a more versatile approach to addressing broader societal challenges.
